final_recommendation: The room converged on a labor enforcement protocol with explicit 'all plants' coverage and audit-cost lock-in, but collapsed on Canada's Chapter 19 red line. USTR rejected any dispute settlement mechanism; Canada refused to sign without it. The deal stalled as a bilateral U.S.-Mexico framework with Canada excluded.
minority_objections: Dairy agriculture sought 10-year quota lock and broader product coverage (7% or butter access) but was sidelined by the Chapter 19 crisis
Auto industry warned that a Mexico-only deal fractures supply chains and makes 75% RVC unenforceable across the integrated North American production network
key_conflicts: Chapter 19 dispute settlement: Canada's non-negotiable red line vs. Congress's absolute rejection
Labor enforcement text delivery: seven agents demanded to see actual draft language before committing, forcing Mexico to produce working text on-screen
Dairy access numbers: Canada offered 5% fluid milk with cheese carved out; U.S. dairy sought 7-10% or butter inclusion
key_concessions: Mexico accelerated enforcement text delivery from Thursday to 5 PM same-day under USTR pressure
Canada moved from 10% dairy rejection to 5% fluid milk acceptance with cheese exclusion
USTR committed to real-time Congressional walkthrough of protocol text (no overnight delays)
Mexico locked monthly audits for 24 months into 75% RVC baseline calculation with no change at quarterly flip
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement must remain intact (stated as 'non-negotiable' and 'red line Canada won't cross')
USTR/Congress: Chapter 19 is 'dead' and 'Congress will not ratify a deal with it intact, full stop'
Congress: enforcement text must explicitly cover 'all plants in supply chain' and lock audit costs into RVC baseline or 'we're killing this in committee'
Labor union: remedies must be tariff suspension + production halt, not fines; 'all plants' must include uncertified suppliers
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Sunset clause / deal duration: supply-chain manufacturers raised 10-year lock necessity for capex commitment, but this was never resolved in the Chapter 19 crisis
Dairy term length: U.S. dairy's request for 10-year quota lock with year-9 renegotiation was dismissed by USTR as 'secondary ask' with no time allocated
Fractured supply chain risk: auto industry's warning that Mexico-only deal makes 75% RVC 'useless' because enforcement becomes unilateral was acknowledged but not addressed
downstream_risk_variables: Canada's Parliament ratification if Chapter 19 is excluded
U.S. Congress ratification if any Chapter 19 mechanism is included (even labor-carved-out version)
Supply-chain compliance cost uncertainty if deal duration remains unspecified
Enforcement protocol implementation: monthly-to-quarterly audit transition mechanics still lack operational detail
Mexico-only deal viability: whether 75% RVC and labor enforcement hold without Canadian participation
uncertainty_notes: Chapter 19 remains binary deadlock with no compromise path identified. Canada proposed labor-sector carve-out (disputes on wages/audits stay in labor chapter, not tribunal), but Congress response was not resolved. Dairy quota term length (10-year lock) and sunset review mechanism were deferred. Auto industry's supply-chain fragmentation concern under Mexico-only scenario was raised but not mitigated.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC with labor-value content drove the entire negotiation structure; seven agents demanded explicit audit-cost lock-in language before committing to retool, and Mexico's protocol text delivery became the meeting's central deadline
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Congress stated 'I can't go back to labor-aligned members and say trust us'; labor union stormed drafting room demanding live proof of 'all plants' language; enforcement text with tariff suspension + production halt became the condition for Congressional ratification
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Canada moved from rejecting 10% to accepting 5% fluid milk with cheese exclusion, but this was acknowledged as politically sensitive ('real market share we can't defend at home') without blocking the deal—Chapter 19 became the actual blocker
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated 'Chapter 19 stays—that's not a negotiating point, it's a red line Canada won't cross' and refused to sign without it; USTR responded 'Chapter 19 is dead—Congress will not ratify a deal with it intact, full stop'; this killed the trilateral package
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply-chain manufacturers raised 10-year lock necessity ('I can't ask my plants to spend that kind of capital on a framework that disappears'), but no compromise mechanism was proposed or adopted—the issue was noted and deferred
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress stated 'I'm not walking a deal to the Hill that looks ratifiable but isn't' and demanded explicit enforcement text before moving; USTR accelerated Mexico's delivery timeline specifically to enable Congressional walkthrough; Canada's Parliament ratification concern shaped dairy and Chapter 19 positions throughout
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto industry and supply-chain manufacturers repeatedly raised retool cost uncertainty tied to audit frequency and compliance baseline ('my suppliers can't quote retool costs without knowing whether they're building for monthly compliance checks'), but this was a constraint acknowledged rather than a driver of concessions
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR stated 'Mexico already has it, and we move the whole deal forward without you' and 'I'm moving forward with Mexico alone and Canada gets left behind'; this bilateral-first framing was the explicit leverage used to pressure Canada on 75% RVC, dairy, and ultimately Chapter 19
